## To the Honored Reader;

I have investigated the *hour of birth* <note>original: "Geburts-Stunde"; likely referring to the astrological "birth chart" of the book's inception.</note> of this book through a cast of *constellated dice* <term>constellated dice (constelirte Würfel): A method of divination or "cleromancy" where dice marked with astrological symbols were thrown to determine favorable conditions or hidden truths.</term>, and the *Daus-Ace* <note>original: "Taus as"; the "Daus" (Two/Deuce) and "As" (Ace) were specific faces of the dice, here personified as the messenger of the parable.</note> tells me this parable. Truth (said the clever beer-seller) was banished into misery, and Lies were set upon their throne: To follow the meaning of this proverb, Truth separated herself from mankind and wandered all alone, naked and wretched. She had not gone far when she stepped onto a high mountain, seeing a great multitude of people passing by; in their midst was a carriage accompanied by kings, princes, and governors, in which sat a beautiful lady, like a reigning queen, who gave orders to the entire company.

Poor Truth stood still as this magnificent crowd passed by; but when the carriage came directly opposite her, the Lies sitting within became aware of her; after she commanded her servants to halt, she told Truth to come closer to her: Then she was

# Preface

...you have lost your administration at court if you kiss the lips of poor Truth: It is not my intention to jest with you in my writing; therefore, read in good faith what I wish to tell you further upon my good conscience.

**GOD**, when He first created man, planted in him a spirit of such capacity <term>capacity: from the Latin 'capacitas,' referring to the intellectual 'vessel' or potential of the soul to receive and hold knowledge</term> that he might know everything, adding to it a great, fervent desire to recognize all things, so that such capacity would not be in vain. This truth is clearly seen in the descendants of Adam; for small children, even before they can speak, are as if eager for that which still seems foreign to them; they do not stop crying and shouting until they get the object into their hands, to properly look at it and feel it, so that they might know to some extent what it is according to the power of their comprehension.

Foolish nurses think that children do all this out of a great desire to play with what they see; but the children themselves testify to the contrary: for when they have outgrown their infancy <note>original: "die Kinder-Schuhe zerrissen," literally "torn their children's shoes," a common 17th-century idiom for moving past the very first stage of childhood</note> and begin to speak, and something new then appears to them, they do not desire to play with it, but rather ask you what it is. In this sense, we do not seek its antiquity, for it is eternal, as it is a knowledge of Divine Wisdom that existed before ancient times or before the creation of the same.

From this time of its revelation, we must trace its antiquity, where our purpose will then be to prove by what moving causes, as well as to whom and when, **GOD** revealed it.

These people have brought forth a certain bastard **Kabbalah**, which consists only of literal constructions and always ends in the very letters with which it begins; its vanity has been recorded in many writings <note>The author is likely criticizing Gematria or Temurah—methods of letter-manipulation—as being superficial "vanity" compared to the "natural" magic he prefers.</note>. However, as for the oldest and nature-conforming statutes or **traditions** of the **Kabbalah**, I embrace them as many holy truths, which remained unknown to most of the **Rabbis** I have read and seen—even to **Rambam** himself. I mean **Rabbi Moses of Egypt** <note>Better known as Maimonides (1135–1204), one of the most influential Torah scholars and philosophers of the Middle Ages.</note>, whom the Jews exalt very highly through their boastful praise, saying: *From Moses unto Moses, there has arisen none like Moses* <note>original Latin: "*a Mose ad Mosen non surrexit sicut Moses*." This famous adage compares Maimonides to the biblical Prophet Moses.</note>.

So that I may deal skillfully with my readers, I say that the **Kabbalah** I accept consists of two parts: <term>the spoken and the being</term> <note>original Greek: "*τοῦ λεγομένου καὶ τοῦ ὄντος*" (tou legomenou kai tou ontos). This distinguishes between the mere verbal transmission and the actual metaphysical reality of the subject.</note>, namely, in the name and the thing itself. The first exists for the sake of the latter.

->E<-

->(Eug. Philal. <note>Pseudonym for Thomas Vaughan (1621–1666), a Welsh alchemist and mystical philosopher.</note>)<-

This is very clear if you consider the various mixtures of the elements and their secret proportions. So much for the **physical part**.

### The Antiquity of Magic. 110

By contrast, Nature is a free spirit and seeks no such fame; she pays heed to no one more than herself. It is told of Mark Antony, a famous but unfortunate Roman, that he sent an emissary throughout the entire world to paint all the beautiful faces so that he might choose the loveliest for himself from among so many magnificent ones. This <term>Chaos</term> <note>In alchemy, "Chaos" refers to the raw, unformed "First Matter" (Prima Materia) that contains all potential elements in a confused state.</note> contains within itself the four elements, which are of contrary properties among themselves; but the wisdom of God has so arranged them that their true order reconciles them with one another. # Preface.

I do not seek to overcome you, but rather to ex-
ercise your understanding; not that you should 
swear yourself to agree with my claims, 
but only compare my conclusions <note>original: "Schluß-Reden," referring to logical deductions or syllogisms</note> with 
nature, and examine their agreement. 
Consider, after all, that stubbornness makes the soul 
a bond-servant, and clips the wings that God 
has given her for soaring and exploring. 
If you will not abandon your Aristotle, 
then let no prejudice hinder your further 
searching. Great is the number of those 
who, if they had not considered themselves 
perfect, might perhaps have attained 
perfection. <note>This reflects a sentiment by the Roman philosopher Seneca: "Many would have reached wisdom if they had not thought they had already reached it."</note> This is my reminder, 
but how pleasing it will be to you, 
I do not know. If you wish only to stomp 
and strike out around you, I will answer, 
as the Cardinal did, that my donkey shall 
also kick out behind. <note>A colloquial way of saying he will respond to insults with equal force.</note> For I care little 
for the judgment of men; we live in a time 
when truth comes close to a miscarriage <note>original: "Mißgebährung," implying that in this era, truth is often born deformed or aborted entirely</note>, 
therefore it is enough that I have appeared 
before her on the day of necessity.

->London, 1650.<-

...were his easy inheritance, but virtue very rarely found an heir. Man had initially—and so have all souls before they enter into this body—**explicit and methodical knowledge** <note>original: "explicitam & methodicam cognitionem"</note>, a revealed and correctly ordered understanding; but as soon as they are veiled by the body, this freedom is already lost, and nothing remains but a rambling, disorderly knowledge of the creature <note>The "creature" here refers to the created, material world as opposed to the Creator.</note>. Thus, there was left to me only a capability without power, and a will to do that which is far beyond my reach. In such distress, I learned various **liberal arts** <note>The traditional academic curriculum of the Middle Ages and Renaissance, consisting of the Trivium (grammar, logic, rhetoric) and the Quadrivium (arithmetic, geometry, music, astronomy).</note> and ran through all these inventions which men, out of foolishness, call sciences. But because these efforts did not serve my purpose, I abandoned such bookish business and considered it a better course to fathom Nature instead of mere opinions. Thereupon I considered within myself that not man, but the world from which he was created, is the initial, direct work of **GOD**; and so that I might arrange my diligence in a proper order, I deemed it fitting to first investigate its origins <note>The "anfänge" or first principles of the universe.</note>, rather than man himself. But because the world in general is too vast for investigation, I decided to take a part instead of the whole, in order to discover its proportions from it. To carry out this plan of mine, I resolved [to observe] the fruits of one spring...

...to consider: here I noticed a great multitude of **earth-growths** <note>German: *Erdgewächſe*. This refers generally to plants, herbs, and all vegetation springing from the soil.</note> that were, in their season, fresh and lovely; but when I looked back at their origin, they were not such things as these earth-growths. I applied this observation to the world and thereby reached the following conclusion: That in the beginning, the world was not such a being as it is now, but was another **seed** or **matter** from which this **edifice** <note>German: *Gebäude*. The author views the physical universe as a constructed building or structure.</note> that hovers before our eyes arose.

Here I proceeded even further with my conclusion and perceived that these seeds, from which the earth-growths spring, must initially have been something other than seeds, as they must have had a previously existing matter from which they were made. But what kind of matter this was supposed to be, I could not guess. Thus, I had to leave off my contemplation and turn instead to experience. I sought the world and passed alongside it, and now inquired after a matter which I was not able to see without **art** <note>German: *Kunſt*. In 17th-century natural philosophy, this often refers to alchemy or the "art" of chemical transformation used to reveal the hidden secrets of nature.</note>; for while Nature very wondrously binds it within her bosom, she also places it before our eyes as nothing other than her own heavenly breath.

In consideration, however, that **GOD** the Almighty is—both in terms of generation and former creation—the sole, actual, and immediate worker <note>The primary agent or craftsman.</note> of this matter, it will not be in vain for us to speak somewhat of Him, so that we may recognize the origin through the **creatures** <note>German: *Creaturen*. In this period, "creatures" refers to all created things in the universe, including minerals and plants, not just animals.</note>, and the creatures through their origin.

This was not a creation—as most people believe—but rather an emanation of the Word, in which was found the Life that is the Light of mankind. This is the light of which Saint John speaks, saying that it shines in the darkness, and the darkness comprehends it not.

"I am that very thing, the Mind, your **God**, more ancient than the moist nature which shone forth out of the shadow." <note>This is a quotation from the *Poimandres*, a foundational text of Hermeticism, where the Divine Mind (Nous) reveals itself to Hermes.</note> That is: I am that same Light, the Mind, your **God**, who is older than the moist nature that has shone forth from the shadow. And Georgius Venetus <note>Francesco Giorgio (1460–1541), a Franciscan friar and Christian Kabbalist, author of *De Harmonia Mundi* (On the Harmony of the World).</note> in his book *On the Harmony of the World*: "Everything that lives, lives because of the heat enclosed within it; from this it is concluded that the nature of heat possesses a vital power within itself, diffused everywhere throughout the world." Understand this to be that fire which **God**—the Inhabitant of the fiery Essence (as Plato says)—commanded to dwell within the already created, coarse and formless *Matter* <note>original: *materia*</note> of heaven and earth, so that it might provide life and form. Just as the spots on the **Moon** are seen by some as earth (though they are more likely just water), and just as no day is so clear that some haze cannot be seen on the **Horizon**: so it goes when people of limited intellect tackle high matters, which only leave a fog behind in their brains. # Preface

Indeed, he possessed such a zealous and sensitive conscience that, when several clergymen requested an interpretation of **Trismegistus** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Egyptian figure credited with writing the Hermetic Corpus, which blended philosophy and mysticism.</note>, he gave them a serious answer and based all true knowledge upon the **Holy Scripture**. In a word, he hated not only godless but also vain arts, and for this reason he lost the favor of the **Queen Mother** <note>Louise of Savoy (1476–1531), mother of King Francis I of France. She was Agrippa’s patroness until he refused to use astrology to predict the king's future.</note>, because he would not accept a position from her in **astrology**. In this science—specifically regarding natural matters such as birth and decay—he possessed exceptional learning. But he knew well that it would be in vain to look for the predetermined outcomes of things in the **planets**, because such things are recorded not in nature, but in the higher tablets of **God’s Providence**.

Now that I have sufficiently proven his sincerity, I will also briefly indicate the causes of his persecution: He was devoted to the **Protestant religion**, and if I had the leisure to cite his works, I would straightaway prove that he did not belong to the **Popish Church**. For in his book *On the Vanity of the Sciences* <note>original: *De incertitudine et vanitate scientiarum atque artium* (1526), a famous work in which Agrippa skeptically attacks the reliability of human knowledge and academic institutions.</note>, he thinks nothing of **monks** and friars, calling them sects of which the early Church in its purity knew nothing. Therefore, his pointed comparison to the **"whore’s cap"** <note>A derogatory reference likely comparing the monastic cowl or church hierarchy to the finery of the Whore of Babylon, a common Reformation-era critique of Catholic ornamentation.</note> still stings the Papists to this day. He also contradicts their images, the invocation of saints, their **purgatory**, and **indulgences**,

# THE MAGICAL SOUL
## HIDDEN.

Building castles in the air is a common proverb among all men, but among the **Peripatetics** <note>The followers of Aristotle, so named because Aristotle reportedly taught while walking around (peripateō). In this context, it refers to the academic establishment of the time, which relied heavily on formal logic.</note> it is a routine occupation.

I have often wondered why the goal and echo of their **philosophy** <note>original: *Welt-Weisheit*; literally "world-wisdom."</note> does not clearly reveal its own falsity. It serves for nothing but a **word-war**; **Mode** and **Figure** <note>original Latin: *Modus* and *Figura*; technical terms for the formal structures of a syllogism in Aristotelian logic.</note> are its two pillars, its **ultimate limit** <note>original Latin: *non ultra*.</note>, and its **sevenfold rule** <note>original: *Heptarchia*; likely referring to the Seven Liberal Arts (Grammar, Rhetoric, Logic, Arithmetic, Geometry, Music, and Astronomy) which dominated the university curriculum.</note> ends in a mere **syllogism** <note>original: *Vernunfft-Schluß*; a logical argument where a conclusion is reached from two or more premises.</note>, and the best professor among them is only a well-trained and practiced brawler. The seven-year studies applied to learning this are seven years of famine; they leave the soul unsatisfied and are more like a dream than that of **Pharaoh**. <note>A biblical reference to the Pharaoh's dream in Genesis 41, where seven lean years of famine devoured the seven years of plenty.</note> For certainly, as far as the stage and dominion of dreams do not exceed the imagination, so the fantasies of such people—which do not surpass their own authors—may sleep in that very same bed.

Such a sect may now rightly be called the <term>people of dreams <gloss>original Greek: δημος ὀνειρῶν (demos oneiron)</gloss></term>, whose **conceptions** <note>original Latin: *Conceptiones*.</note> are not based on even the slightest ground of proof found in nature, and yet they strive to force nature into their own devised—

# THE HIDDEN MAGICAL SOUL.
## <note>original Latin title: *Anima Magica Abscondita*</note>

Building castles in the air is a common proverb among all people, but among the **Peripatetics** <note>The followers of Aristotle. In this era, "Peripatetic" was often used as a derogatory term for university scholars who relied on ancient logic rather than experimental or spiritual insight.</note> it is a customary occupation.

I have often wondered that the purpose and the echo of their **worldly wisdom** <note>original: *Welt-Weisheit*; a common term for philosophy.</note> did not clearly reveal its own falsehood. It serves only for a **war of words**; **Mode** and **Figure** <note>original: *Modus* and *Figura*; technical terms in formal logic referring to the structure of a syllogism.</note> are its two pillars, its **limit** <note>original Latin: *non ultra*; literally "nothing beyond."</note>, and its **rule of seven** <note>original Latin: *Heptarchia*; here likely referring to the seven liberal arts that formed the core of medieval and Renaissance education.</note> ends in a logical conclusion, and the best professor among them is only a well-trained and practiced quarreler. The seven-year **studies** applied to learning it are seven years of hunger: they leave the soul unsatisfied and are more like a dream than that of Pharaoh <note>A reference to the biblical story in Genesis 41, where Pharaoh dreams of seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine.</note>. For certainly, as far as the stage and dominion of dreams does not exceed the imagination, so may the fantasies of such people—who do not surpass their authors—sleep upon the same bed.

Such a sect can rightly be called a **common dream** <note>original Greek: *δημός ὄνειρος* (dēmos oneiros).</note>, whose **conceptions** are not based on the slightest ground of proof found in nature, and yet they take pains to force nature onto their own...

Since nature in general—that is, according to its active and passive parts, namely **Matter** and **Form**—together with the human soul, is the main foundation upon which a philosophy is to be built; and since this Aristotle has been made into such a saint by his followers that the **clergymen of Cologne** <note>A reference to the Scholastic theologians of the University of Cologne, who were famous for their rigid adherence to Aristotelian philosophy, often calling him the "forerunner of Christ in natural matters."</note> were moved to consider him a forerunner of Christ in the works of nature, just as John <note>John the Baptist</note> was in the works of grace: I will further examine his **Definitions** and acknowledge with thanks whatever use I find. 

First, one might think I would be indebted to this man for informing me that nature is a **beginning**. Indeed, in such a way I could also tell the reader that the passive spirit of the truly wise is a "beginning"; but if I do not express to him what kind of essence it is, I could let him search for ten years and he would still not recognize, without supernatural assistance, what or where it is.

Again, you might object: he shows me not only that nature is a beginning, but also a **Form**, and that therefore, consequently, the **Form** is nature. That is the same exchange of words; he keeps me imprisoned in a circle of knowledge and resolves absolutely nothing. Furthermore, the word **Form** <note>original: *Forma*</note>, according to the proper understanding of the language, means only the outward symmetry or shape of a thing. ### On the Spirit of Nature, etc. 258

It is sufficiently obvious to all those gifted with good understanding and suitable vessels to employ it, that every being in the world is subject to a certain kind of movement: Animals have, besides their external progress, their internal movements of life; the heavens are turned by that which the <term>Peripatetics</term> <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, often criticized by alchemists for being too theoretical and focused on logic rather than physical experimentation.</note> call <term>motion</term> <note>original Latin: *motio*</note>, regarding which I might incidentally mention that it arises from an internal beginning and not from those supposed <term>Intelligences</term> <note>original: *Intelligentien*; celestial spirits or angels that medieval scholars believed literally moved the planetary spheres.</note>. # On the Spirit of Nature, etc. 274

That is: There are, as we have said, four **elements**, without the perfect knowledge of which nothing can be accomplished in **Magic**. However, each of these is threefold, so that in this way the **Fourfold** <note>original: *Quaternarius*; the number four, representing the foundational structure of the physical world.</note> completes the **Twelvefold** <note>original: *Duodenarius*; likely referring to the twelve signs of the Zodiac or the full expansion of elemental properties.</note>, and by proceeding through the **Sevenfold** <note>original: *Septenarius*; the seven planetary influences.</note> to the **Tenfold** <note>original: *Denarius*; the number ten, representing a return to unity and the Divine.</note>, it may reach the highest Unity, upon which all power and wonderful effects depend.

Now, according to the first order, the **elements** are pure; they are neither compounded nor changed, nor do they suffer any mixing, but are incorruptible. They are not those substances *from* which things are made, but rather the mediums *through* which the powers of all natural things are brought to fruition and effect. Their powers and virtues cannot be sufficiently investigated or explored by anyone, because they perform "all in all" <note>This implies a pantheistic or panentheistic view where these pure forces are active in every part of creation.</note>. Whoever does not know these will never reach any practice of wonderful effects.

According to the second order, the **elements** are impure, numerous, and manifold; however, they can be led back through **Art** <note>In this context, "Art" refers to alchemy or the "Great Work" of purifying base matter into its spiritual essence.</note> into a pure simplicity. Once they have been brought to this state, they possess such power that they surpass everything and bring perfection to all hidden and manifest operations of nature.

The **elements** of the third order are not elements in themselves, but are many and manifold **de-compounded substances** <term>decomposita</term> <note>These are complex, "doubly-compounded" materials that have been broken down and transformed; they are the physical substances we interact with in the world.</note>; they are also interchangeable among themselves. They are the infallible medium, and for this reason, they are called the **Middle-Nature**, or the

<meta>catchword: Soul</meta>

# On the Spirit of Nature, etc. 275

...be called the **soul of the middle nature**: there are very few who understand their deeply hidden secrets. # On the Spirit of Nature, etc. 274

That is: There are, therefore, as we have stated, four **elements**, without a perfect knowledge of which nothing can be accomplished in **magic**. However, each one of these is threefold, so that in this manner the <term>Quaternarius (the number four)</term> completes the <term>Duodenarius (the number twelve)</term> <note>This refers to the four elements—Fire, Air, Water, Earth—each existing in three states, totaling twelve.</note>; and proceeding through the <term>Septenarius (the number seven)</term> toward the <term>Denarius (the number ten)</term>, it may arrive at the highest **Unity**, upon which all power and wondrous operations depend.

According to the **first order**, the elements are pure; they are neither composed nor changed, nor do they suffer any mixing. Instead, they are incorruptible. They are not the things *from which* the powers of all natural things are produced, but rather the things *through which* those powers are brought into effect and operation. Their powers and virtues cannot be sufficiently traced or explored by anyone, for they perform all in all. Whoever does not know these will never attain any practice of wondrous effects.

According to the **second order**, the elements are impure, numerous, and manifold. However, through the **Art** <note>In this context, "Art" refers to Alchemy or Hermetic science.</note> they are led back into a pure simplicity. Once they have been brought to this state, they possess such power that they surpass all things and grant perfection to all hidden and manifest operations of nature.

The elements of the **third order** are not elements in themselves, but are numerous and manifold <term>Decomposita (complex composites)</term> which are changeable even among themselves. They are the infallible medium; therefore, they are called the **Middle-Nature**, or the **soul**

...do you seek so anxiously, you mortals?
You wretched ones, why do you plague your minds with such unending worries? What presumption blinds you? Because everything is **in** you—not **of** you—everything which you seek outside of yourselves and not within yourselves. It is a peculiar vice of the common masses that they despise what is their own and always long for what is foreign. By this "own-ness" <note>German: *Eigenthümliche*. This refers to the innate spiritual gifts or the "Image of God" within a person, rather than material property.</note> I mean that which is bestowed upon us; for from our own selves we have nothing good, but where we have something good, we have it from Him who alone is good. Conversely, what evil we have, we have taken upon ourselves from a foreign evil through disobedience. 

Thus, man has nothing as his own property from himself except the evil he possesses. The good that he has from the Good One is not from himself; rather, by way of bestowal <term>Zueignungs-weise: a theological term for "imputation" or "appropriation," where a quality belonging to God is granted to the human soul.</term>, he holds it as his own from the Good. Life appears to us (albeit darkly) as a light in the darkness, which does not originate from ourselves, but from Him to whom it belongs. He, who dwells in a light that no one can approach <note>A reference to 1 Timothy 6:16.</note>, has planted it within us, so that in His light we might see light <note>A reference to Psalm 36:9.</note> and thereby surpass the other creatures; for in such a way we become like Him, because He has given us a **spark** <term>Füncklein: The "Scintilla" or "Spark of the Soul," a concept in mysticism suggesting a tiny, indestructible part of the divine remains within the human soul.</term> of His light. Therefore, we should seek the truth not in ourselves, but in the **Image of God** that is within us.

# On the Spirit of Nature, etc.

This is the very person to whom the Rosicrucians <term>Rosenkreuzer: members of a secret philosophical society focused on spiritual alchemy and the transformation of the soul.</term> have given the name of a "Wise Man," and from whose writings they have borrowed most of their instructions *to a certain German Candidate* <note>original: "ad Candidatum quendam Germaniæ."</note>. "True Knowledge," he says, "does not occur until the soul, having been presented with a comparison between the eternal and the fleeting—between life and destruction—chooses to be joined with the higher spirit <note>original: "anima cum animo conjungi." In this context, *anima* refers to the vital soul/life-force and *animus* to the higher, rational spirit or mind.</note>, drawn by a greater delight in the latter than in the body. From this knowledge the mind <note>original: "mens"</note> arises, and the voluntary separation from the body begins; for the soul—beholding on the one hand the foulness and destruction of the body, and on the other the excellence and perpetual happiness of the spirit—longs to be connected with that spirit (under the direction of the divine breath). Neglecting the body completely, so that it seeks only what it sees decreed by God for salvation and glory, the body is then compelled to yield to the union of the two now united. 

This is that wonderful transformation of the Sages—of the body into Spirit, and the Spirit into body—concerning which it is left said to us by the Wise: 'Make the fixed volatile, and the volatile fixed, so that you may have our mastery' <note>original: "Fac fixum volatile, & volatile fixum." A foundational alchemical maxim: to spiritualize the material and materialize the spiritual.</note>: understand this to mean, make the stubborn body tractable, so that by the excellence of the spirit agreeing with the soul, it becomes a most constant body, able to withstand all tests. For gold is proven by fire, by which everything that is not gold is rejected. Oh, most excellent gold of the Sages, with which the sons of Wisdom are enriched—not that gold which is minted into coins!"

**Testimonies of several highly esteemed *philosophers*** concerning the first *matter* 113. and following <note>original: "Philosophorum... Materia... sqq." The "first matter" (materia prima) is the formless base substance required for alchemical transmutation.</note>

**Harmony between nature and the *Gospel***, is proven from the *Chinese* monument of *Kimcim*, a priest from *Judea*, 76. and following <note>original: "Evangelio... Sinesischen Gedenckmal... sq." This refers to the Nestorian Stele (found in 1625), an 8th-century monument in Xi'an. Early modern scholars used it to argue that Christianity had reached China in antiquity. "Kimcim" likely refers to the monk Adam (Jingjing), who is credited with the text on the stele.</note>
